It is the Yōki Shrine of {{ill|Ikeda district|ja|池田郡|qid=Q11552165}} in {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}}, listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki}}. Yōki Shrine is the only Shikinaisha in Ikeda District of Mino Province. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine status}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== History ===
The date of establishment is unknown, but the {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}} records that it became a government-supported shrine in the 2nd year of {{ill|Kashō|de|Kachō|es|Kashō|fa|کاشو (دوره)|fr|Ère Kashō|ia|Kajo|id|Kajō|ja|嘉祥|ko|가쇼 (848년)|ru|Кадзё (848—851)|simple|Kashō (early Heian period)|sr|Кашо (ера)|tr|Kashō|uk|Кадзьо (ненґо)|zh|嘉祥 (日本)|zh_yue|嘉祥 (年號)|qid=Q1373157}} ({{ill|849|ab|849|af|849|als|849|am|849 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|849|ar|849|ary|849|arz|849|ast|849|avk|849|az|849|azb|۸۴۹ (میلادی)|bcl|849|be|849|be_x_old|849|bg|849|bn|৮৪৯|bpy|মারি ৮৪৯|br|849|bs|849.|ca|849|cdo|849 nièng|ceb|849|ckb|٨٤٩|crh|849|cs|849|csb|849|cv|849|cy|849|da|849|de|849|el|849|eml|849|eo|849|es|849|et|849|eu|849|fa|۸۴۹ (میلادی)|fi|849|fo|849|fr|849|frr|849|fy|849|ga|849|gan|849年|gd|849|gl|849|he|849|hi|849|hr|849.|ht|849 (almanak jilyen)|hu|849|hy|849|id|849|ilo|849|io|849|it|849|ja|849年|jv|849|ka|849|kaa|849|kk|849 жыл|ko|849년|la|849|lb|849|lij|849|lmo|849|lt|849 m.|lv|849. gads|map_bms|849|mdf|849|mg|849|mhr|849|mk|849|mr|इ.स. ८४९|mrj|849 и|ms|849|mzn|۸۴۹|nah|849|nap|849|nds|849|new|सन् ८४९|nl|849|nn|849|no|849|nrm|849|nso|849|oc|849|or|୮୪୯|os|849-æм аз|pl|849|pnb|849|pt|849|qu|849|ro|849|ru|849 год|rue|849|sa|८४९|scn|849|sd|849ع|se|849|sh|849.|shn|849|si|849|simple|849|sk|849|sl|849|smn|849|sq|849|sr|849|su|849|sv|849|sw|849|tg|Соли 849|th|พ.ศ. 1392|tk|849|tl|849|tly|849|tr|849|tt|849 ел|uk|849|ur|849ء|uz|849|vec|849|vi|849|war|849|wuu|849年|xmf|849|zh|849年|zh_min_nan|849 nî|zh_yue|849年|qid=Q23902}}).

During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was known as “Yagi Daimyōjin” or “Yamata Myōjin.” When it was designated a gōsha in the 6th year of {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was renamed Yōki Shrine.

=== Enshrined deity ===
*Yōki Ōkami
*:It is unknown what kind of deity Yōki Ōkami is. One theory holds that this region has many rivers flowing from the {{ill|Ibuki Mountains|Q4387713|qid=Q4387713}} and {{ill|Mount Ikeda|Q981510|qid=Q981510|lt=Mount Ikeda}}, including the {{ill|Kasu River|Q11604491|qid=Q11604491|lt=Kasu River}}, and that the god of these rivers was enshrined here. Another theory links the name to “eight forks” (yamata), interpreting the deity as a god of branching paths.
*:The Shrine Directory lists {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}} as the enshrined deity.

=== Access ===
*Approximately 2 km from {{ill|Mino-Hongō Station|Q11609239|qid=Q11609239}} on the {{ill|Yoro Railway|Q11666892|qid=Q11666892}}.
